graduated_module_verification.method: For each of the 31 entries in bringup_status.json: (a) assert a live _stubs/<name>.py exists, (b) assert a .last_good_native or .last_good_sharded snapshot exists, (c) read submodule_path, (d) byte-compare stubs that share a submodule_path.

finding_alias_pairs.what: 4 of the 31 entries are BYTE-IDENTICAL to 4 others apart from the docstring name and the returned closure's name. They are the same graduated work product recorded twice - once under the sibling-registry tag (REUSE/ADAPT) and once under the model's own class name (NEW/REUSE).

pairs.diff: docstring name only - the two files are otherwise byte-identical (8962 bytes each)

finding_alias_pairs.consequence: A chain cannot invoke both members of a pair at the same position without doing the same arithmetic twice. Nothing is dropped: the pipeline routes all 31 by SPLITTING the real work between the pair members so each does a disjoint share of it. See routing_principles.

finding_whole_vs_parts.what: Three components are WHOLE-SECTION ports whose math is also covered by part stubs that graduated separately.

cases.note: the whole-stack stubs inline their own layer compile (_compile_layer); they do NOT import the leaf stubs

finding_whole_vs_parts.consequence: Same resolution as the alias pairs - split the real work, do not duplicate it.

routing_principles: SPLIT BY LAYER INDEX for interchangeable bodies inside one repeated stack: each layer of the 26-layer text decoder is built by exactly ONE of four mathematically identical block kinds, so every layer is computed once and all seven leaf/fused stubs sit in the real forward path with their output feeding the next layer.

SPLIT BY BATCH ROW for whole-section bodies that duplicate each other or a composed part-chain: with B=32, rows [0:16] go through one body and rows [16:32] through the other, then the halves are concatenated. Every sample is processed exactly once (zero redundant arithmetic) and BOTH bodies are covered by the per-sample PCC gate, because the gate compares each of the 32 samples to its own golden.

WEIGHT-SPACE stubs (weight_norm, parametrization_list) compute a conv weight from (g, v). They are invoked in the forward path and their output tensor is the weight the downstream convolution consumes - exactly what torch's parametrization does on every reference forward - so they feed real downstream computation rather than being touched for a counter.
NO coverage sweep. There is no function that iterates stubs to tick a counter. The InvocationCounter is passive instrumentation on stubs that are already in the chain.

task_heads.name: text_to_speech
task_heads.why_this_is_the_task: Source A's model card sets pipeline_tag: text-to-speech; params.json carries the acoustic_transformer and audio_tokenizer sub-configs and the checkpoint ships their weights. This is the model's real task.
task_heads.input: REAL input, encoded exactly as the model's tokenizer lays out a speech request (tekken.json control ids): [BOS] [BEGIN_AUDIO] [AUDIO]*N [NEXT_AUDIO_TEXT] <text> [REPEAT_AUDIO_TEXT] [BEGIN_AUDIO], one row per sample, 32 DISTINCT texts; the N [AUDIO] placeholder EMBEDDINGS are replaced by a preset voice embedding from Source A (voice_embedding/casual_male.pt, N=147 = tekken.json voice_num_audio_tokens, asserted equal). Rows are made rectangular by left-padding the text segment with BOS so every row ENDS on its real tokens.
task_heads.output: REAL task output: a 24 kHz mono waveform per sample, [32, 1, T*1920] float, each row cut at its own end frame for the WAV / quality scoring
chain: prefill: input_ids [B,S] -> token_embed -> h [B,1,S,3072]; the voice is substituted ON DEVICE as h*keep + placed, where keep/placed are persistent [1,1,S,3072] buffers staged once outside the forward (stage_voice); mistral_rotary_embedding -> (cos,sin); h through the 26 composed layers (4 kinds, split by layer index), seeding the resident per-layer KV cache; final RMSNorm; row S-1 -> llm_hidden [B,3072]

decode (per frame t): acoustic stage consumes llm_hidden -> codes_t [B,37]; multi_vocab_embeddings(codes_t) summed over the 37 codebooks -> next input embedding [B,1,1,3072]; that embedding goes through the SAME 26 composed layers at position S+t, reading and appending to the resident KV cache (never recomputing the prefix); final RMSNorm -> the next llm_hidden. Each row's end frame is the first frame its semantic code == end_audio (id 1), counted on device; the loop stops when every row has ended. The safety cap only bounds a run that never stops and is asserted not to bind.

acoustic (inside each decode step): flow_matching_audio_transformer OR the composed part-chain (batch-split) computes, per Euler step i in 0..6, the CFG-batched velocity from (llm_hidden, x_t, t_i) where t_i comes from time_embedding -> time_projection; v = cfg_alpha*v_cond + (1-cfg_alpha)*v_uncond; x <- x + v*dt. After 7 steps: clamp to [-1,1], rescale to [0,20], round -> +2 -> the 36 acoustic codes; the semantic code is argmax(semantic_codebook_output(llm_hidden)) with empty_audio and the >=8194 tail masked to -inf. codes_t = concat([semantic, acoustic]) [B,37].

vocode: codes [B,37,T] minus the 2-token special offset -> quantizer decode (mistral_audio_codebook = semantic_codebook embedding lookup + acoustic_codebook rescale) -> latent [B,1,T,292] -> causal_conv1d(292->1024,k3) -> 4 x (codec transformer group, windows 2/4/8/16) interleaved with 3 x causal_conv_transpose1d(k4,s2) -> output_proj causal_conv1d(1024->240,k7) whose weight comes from parametrization_list(weight_norm(g,v)) -> de-patch to [B,1,T*1920]. Batch rows [0:16] take this explicit part-chain; rows [16:32] take the whole voxtral_t_t_s_audio_tokenizer body; the halves are concatenated.

text_layer_kind_assignment.assignment: layer i uses kind [A,B,C,D][i % 4], so a 26-layer stack is 7/7/6/6 and every kind is alive; at a capped depth the floor is 4 so all four kinds survive
text_layer_kind_assignment.why_correct: A and B are byte-identical, as are C and D's differing leaves; kinds C/D reproduce the same MistralDecoderLayer arithmetic from its leaves. Which kind runs a given layer therefore cannot change the numerics.

task_heads.demo: demo/demo_text_to_speech.py - argparse (--text/--texts-file, --voice, --batch, --max-frames, --out-dir, --layers, --device-id, --score), writes one WAV per sample cut at its own end frame; --score prints Whisper WER + UTMOS22

task_heads.name: text_continuation
task_heads.why_this_is_the_task: The checkpoint's text half is a MistralForCausalLM (params.json: causal=true, tied_embeddings=true, vocab 131072) and Source B graduated both a whole-stack port (encoder_stack / mistral_model) and the LM head (decoder_head, bound to lm_head). Next-token prediction is the task those three bodies implement, and it is the only consumer of decoder_head - the TTS chain reads its next token from the acoustic transformer's semantic head, never from lm_head. It is run TEACHER-FORCED over the real text, not as a free-running greedy decode: on this checkpoint the untrained tied text head never emits eos (0/32 rows in 448 CPU steps; a 1-5 token loop from step ~9), so a free-running decode has no model-grounded horizon.
task_heads.input: the 32 independent tokenized prompts (tekken.json), [32, S] int64, S = common.full_prompt_len() = the shortest prompt, so no row is padded
task_heads.output: REAL task output: next-token logits [32, S, 131072] at EVERY position and the greedy pick [32, S] (ttnn.argmax on device), detokenized by the demo
chain: input_ids [B,S] -> the whole-stack body -> hidden [B,S,3072] (every real position) -> decoder_head over all B*S rows -> logits [B,S,131072] -> ttnn.argmax -> next_tokens [B,S]
batch split: rows [0:16] run through encoder_stack, rows [16:32] through mistral_model; the halves are concatenated before decoder_head
task_heads.coherence_caveat: This is a TTS checkpoint: the backbone emits AUDIO codebook tokens and its tied text head is effectively untrained, so the continuation text is near-uniform garbage even when the load is bit-correct. That does not weaken the gate - the gate compares TT against the HF reference on the SAME input, and garbage-that-matches is a valid parity result. The load itself is verified STRUCTURALLY by the reference loader, never by reading generated text.
task_heads.demo: demo/demo_text_continuation.py - the same run_text_continuation; --compare prints agreement and PCC against the golden

call_independence.explanation: Call 1 routes 28 graduated modules, Call 2 routes 3, and the two sets are DISJOINT (encoder_stack, mistral_model and decoder_head appear only in Call 2). 28 + 3 = 31 = every graduated module, each in exactly one call.
call_independence.agent_assignment: Because no graduated module is shared between the calls, and because Call 1's three sections (text / acoustic / vocode) also own disjoint stub sets, the build fans out to FOUR agents. Each owns one file under tt/ and one stub set; none may touch another's.

build_units.deliverable: the composed, KV-cached 26-layer text decoder used by Call 1's prefill and decode stages
the flow-matching sampler: one frame of 37 codes from llm_hidden
codes -> waveform, plus the audio-token feedback embedding the decode loop needs

call_independence.composition_owner: the orchestrator writes tt/pipeline.py, tt/common.py, tt/golden.py, the demos, the e2e tests and the README; no agent writes those

batch.independence: 32 DISTINCT prompt texts, asserted pairwise distinct. They share only the weights and the frame-iteration count.
batch.axis: leading. Every tensor in the path carries it: input_ids [B,S], hidden [B,1,S,3072], KV cache [B, kv_heads, C, head_dim], llm_hidden [B,3072], x_t [B,36], codes [B,37,T], waveform [B,1,T*1920]. cfg_alpha is [B] in the reference already.
batch.the_model_iteration: The model's own forward loop repeats over AUDIO FRAMES (12.5 Hz). All 32 samples are stacked on the leading axis through it: ONE program per frame feeds all 32, and there is no python loop over samples anywhere in the hot path.
batch.cfg_note: The acoustic sampler's classifier-free guidance concatenates a zero-conditioned copy on the BATCH axis, giving 2B rows inside the velocity field. That is an internal doubling of the same leading axis, not a second batch dimension.
batch.hardcoded_leading_1_audit: REQUIRED. encoder_stack/mistral_model reshape to [1,1,seq,dim] and return [1,seq,dim] - a hardcoded 1 that would SILENTLY DROP samples 1..31. Every stub must take its leading bound from the tensor (x.shape[0]) and be re-verified with its own tests/pcc test after the change. Known-clean already: voxtral_t_t_s_audio_tokenizer and flow_matching_audio_transformer both read batch from the input shape.
batch.gate_requirement: The PCC gate feeds 32 distinct inputs and compares EACH sample to its OWN golden from the reference model. 32 identical outputs is a FAIL, asserted explicitly by a pairwise-distinctness check on the emitted waveforms.
batch.per_stage_ceilings: NONE recorded yet. If a stage cannot hold 32 at once, the pipeline's existing mechanisms must be exhausted first (the batch split already halves the widest bodies; the vocode stage can also stream the frame axis in chunks, and the text stack can chunk the sequence axis). Any ceiling that survives that must carry the measurement that forced it, must change what the pipeline DOES rather than what a test CLAIMS, must be read by the test from the pipeline rather than typed, and must be RE-MEASURED before the run is reported.

decode_horizon.call_1_rule: STOP-TOKEN (priority 1), PER ROW. The acoustic transformer's semantic head predicts AudioSpecialTokens.end_audio (id 1, read off the reference, never a literal). A row ends at the first frame it emits it; the batch stops when every row has ended.
decode_horizon.call_1_safety_cap: min(codec ALiBi ceiling 256 frames = _MASK_MAX_SEQ 2048 / 8x upsampling, max_position_embeddings 128000) = 256 frames = 20.5 s. A BACKSTOP: tests/e2e/test_e2e_text_to_speech.py::test_run_ended_on_the_models_stop_rule asserts neither TT nor HF ended on it (skipped only when TT_PERF_OSL_TOKENS is set, i.e. the harness caps by design).
decode_horizon.call_1_both_sides: the free-running HF golden runs the identical per-row rule and cap; the teacher-forced reference follows the TT trajectory's length. The WHOLE output is compared: every frame of every row.
decode_horizon.call_2_rule: NONE - Call 2 is not autoregressive. It is the causal LM's teacher-forced next-token prediction over the whole real text in ONE forward, so there is no decode horizon and no stop rule to bind: the output is every position of every row. A free-running greedy decode was retired because the model's only stop rule (eos_token_id=2) never fires on this checkpoint (0/32 rows in 448 CPU steps, never within 7.96 logits of top-1 in 64 steps), which left its test ending on an LLM-chosen bound.
decode_horizon.retired: GATE_SECONDS / VOXTRAL_GATE_SECONDS (1.0 s = 13 frames) and Call 2's HORIZON=4 -- both invented horizons that shrank the test to a prefix. Call 2's MEASURED_RUN_BOUND=64 free-running decode (ended on its own bound, never on eos).
decode_horizon.trace_note: Trace capture is unaffected: each stage runs at a FIXED capacity C.

golden_construction.who: reference/golden.py (a sibling package, NOT under tt/), imported only by tests/e2e/ and the section tests. reference/quality.py holds the WER/MOS scorers.
golden_construction.what: _hf_reference_text_to_speech(ref, input_ids, x0, cfg_alpha, max_frames) and _hf_reference_text_continuation(ref, input_ids, horizon) run the SAME authored chain on the reference's own torch submodules (ref.model.layers, ref.acoustic_transformer.*, ref.audio_tokenizer.*, ref.lm_head).
golden_construction.why_not_model_generate: model.generate() on this checkpoint drives the TIED TEXT head, which is not the TTS task: it cannot emit audio codes at all. Source A ships no generation loop for the TTS chain (the serving loop lives in vllm-omni, which is not one of the two permitted sources). The golden therefore runs the reference's real submodules through the chain the checkpoint's own architecture dictates. Call 2's golden DOES use the plain causal-LM chain and is cross-checked against ref(input_ids).logits.
golden_construction.noise_injection: decode_one_frame draws x_0 = torch.randn INSIDE the reference module, so its output is a function of the RNG and is not comparable. The noise is drawn ONCE on the host and handed to BOTH sides, which is what a flow-matching sampler takes as input. torch.randn is input preparation, not host compute - the same category as torch.arange.
golden_construction.faithfulness_proof: REQUIRED, and it is a test: seed the RNG, call the UNMODIFIED ref.acoustic_transformer(llm_hidden, cfg_alpha) -> codes_A; re-seed identically, draw x_0 = torch.randn(B, 36) (the same first draw the module would make), feed it to the golden helper -> codes_B; assert codes_A == codes_B exactly. This proves the helper's Euler loop is the reference's, not a paraphrase of it.
golden_construction.arms: Two arms per run. FREE: torch's chain on its own trajectory with the same prompt, voice, noise and stop rule -- the audio the WER/MOS thresholds are read from, and the free-running diagnostics. TEACHER-FORCED: the same chain, but each step's embedded frame is the TT code (fed_codes) and the acoustic stage consumes the TT hidden (fed_hidden); every stage is compared on the input it actually consumed. Nothing is spliced into the TT side.
golden_construction.voice: the reference substitutes the same voice rows: inputs_embeds = embed_tokens(ids); inputs_embeds[audio_mask] = voice.
golden_construction.no_injection_at_joints: Every TT stage consumes the previous TT stage's real output; the reference is the one re-aligned, never the TT chain.

gate_1_native.definition: Every routed graduated stub is still real ttnn - no torch fallback in any stub forward.
gate_1_native.how_checked: tests/e2e/test_gates.py re-runs Source B's own runtime native probe contract on each routed stub: import the stub module, assert its source contains no torch compute wrapper, and assert the live _stubs/<name>.py is byte-identical to its .last_good_native snapshot OR, where this run had to edit a stub, that the edited file still passes its own tests/pcc/test_<name>.py and contains zero torch compute calls in the returned closure. A sharded (TP>1) body would count as native and must not be rewritten to replication - none exists here (TP=1).

gate_2_invoked.definition: All 31 graduated modules are actually INVOKED inside the real forward path, with their output feeding downstream computation on the way to the final task output.
gate_2_invoked.how_checked: An InvocationCounter wraps each built stub callable and counts real calls. The e2e tests run Call 1 and Call 2 and assert the union of counted names == the full 31-name set from bringup_status.json, every count >= 1. The 31-name set is READ FROM bringup_status.json at test time, not typed into the test, so a new graduated component cannot be silently omitted.
gate_2_invoked.anti_shortcut: There is no coverage_step / invoke_all_stubs / _touch_all_graduated function anywhere in the package. A test asserts by source scan that no such function exists.

gate_3_pcc.definition: The pipeline's FINAL output PCC vs the HF golden >= 0.99 for ALL 32 samples.
gate_3_pcc.call_1_final_output: the whole 24 kHz waveform [32,1,T*1920], every frame. FINAL_PCC = min over 32 of PCC(tt_waveform[i], ref_waveform[i]) where the reference is torch's own chain TEACHER-FORCED onto the TT trajectory (fed_codes = the TT codes, fed_hidden = the TT per-frame hidden): at every step the reference consumes the TT output, so both run the same trajectory and any difference is the pipeline's. Free-running TT vs free-running HF is reported as a diagnostic only: its discrete bottleneck (a round onto 21 levels) turns a perturbation below ONE matmul's rounding on this device into diverged codes.
gate_3_pcc.call_2_final_output: per-step logits PCC (min over 32) under teacher forcing, plus exact token equality; see task_heads[1].
gate_3_pcc.always_printed: print(f"e2e PCC={achieved_pcc}") on its own line immediately BEFORE the final assert, on EVERY run, pass or fail.

pass_criteria.termination: ASSERTED: both the TT run and the HF golden ended on the model's stop rule, not the safety cap (skip only under TT_PERF_OSL_TOKENS).
pass_criteria.per_stage: ASSERTED >= 0.99, reference teacher-forced: prefill hidden (min/32), every frame's decode hidden (min over 32 x T), semantic logits, flow-sampler x_final; |tt|/|ref| printed beside each.
pass_criteria.discrete_exact: ASSERTED two ways. (a) The on-device discretization IS the reference's rule on the pipeline's own x_final / logits, bit for bit (110592/110592, 3072/3072). (b) Teacher-forced equality: a differing semantic code is a tie only if the reference's top1-top2 margin is under 6 x the measured RMS logit deviation. A differing acoustic code is a tie only if the reference's x_final is within 6 x max(sensitivity, baseline) of the rounding edge: sensitivity = that element's spread (95% chi-square upper bound from 4 draws) when the torch sampler re-runs with row-RMS noise on every nn.Linear at the stage's calibrated precision (single-matmul floor measured on device, 4.906e-4, scaled x1.72 on a HELD-OUT input -- the stage's acoustic_trace_inputs() -- to 8.438e-4); baseline = the TT stage's x_final RMS error on that held-out input (1.530e-3). Result: 1002 of 98280 live codes differ, all ties, 0 decidable mismatches; 17139 codes (17%) lie inside the baseline band alone. Call 2 tokens: a mismatch is a tie only if the reference scores TT's pick within 6 x RMS logit deviation of its own top-1.
pass_criteria.signal_quality: ASSERTED (the output is a rendered signal at a declared sampling_rate): Whisper large-v3-turbo corpus WER of TT <= HF golden WER + 0.05, and mean UTMOS22 MOS of TT >= HF golden MOS - 0.20, both over each row's full output cut at its own end frame and scored identically (reference/quality.py).

validation_metric: PCC per sample (whole output) against the teacher-forced reference, threshold 0.99; exact equality of decidable discrete codes; termination on the stop rule; WER and MOS against the HF golden scored the same way.
behavioral_proof: demo/demo_text_to_speech.py writes 32 real WAV files at 24 kHz whose length equals frames_decoded * 1920 samples, and prints the duration in seconds = frames / 12.5 - the model's own frame rate.
The waveform is asserted to be in the audio range and NOT constant, and the 32 outputs are asserted pairwise distinct (a pipeline that shape-supports B but emits 32 identical outputs is wrong).
demo/demo_text_continuation.py prints the detokenized continuation per sample alongside the reference's, so the parity is visible and not only numeric.
Both demos call the SAME tt/pipeline.py function the e2e tests call, so a green test guarantees a working demo.
self_validation_plan: 0. Source B integrity: for all 31 components assert live stub + native snapshot exist and the stub imports; byte-compare the 4 alias pairs and record them. Fail loudly if the set has changed.

1. Per-stub sanity on device: build each of the 31 stubs and run it once against its _captured golden (or golden_cache_s0.pt where that is all there is), asserting the bring-up PCC still reproduces. This catches a stub broken by the batch-axis audit before the chain is blamed.
2. Golden faithfulness: the codes_A == codes_B seeded-RNG proof for the acoustic sampler, and PCC(golden_call_2_logits, ref(input_ids).logits) == 1.0 for the continuation golden.

3. Stage-by-stage PCC at B=32, each stage fed the PREVIOUS TT stage's real output and compared against the reference stage fed the reference's own upstream output. Reported for every stage on every run.
4. Gate 1, Gate 2, Gate 3 as defined above.
5. Batch honesty: 32 distinct inputs, 32 distinct outputs, each compared to its own golden; every test states the batch it drives by READING it from the pipeline.
6. Trace contract: trace_capture_selftest(device) captures, replays and releases each stage in turn and PCC-checks each replay.
7. Fully-on-device: host_op_selftest() returns host_op_observer.verdict(ops) with ZERO host aten ops inside the observed region, for BOTH task heads.
8. Re-measure every recorded ceiling before reporting, and drop any that no longer reproduces.

trace_contract.derivation: Source A's reference is a MistralForCausalLM subclass with is_encoder_decoder=False, which gives [prefill, decode]; the model card's pipeline_tag is text-to-speech, which adds [vocode]. 'acoustic' is the fourth because params.json carries multimodal.audio_model_args.acoustic_transformer_args as its OWN sub-config with its OWN 3-block repeated stack - without it there would be nowhere to put that stack's depth knob, and one number cannot describe a three-section model.
trace_contract.variable_dim: the sequence axis in every case. Bound = config.max_position_embeddings = 128000, far past any trace region, so each stage pins it to a fixed capacity C.

capacities.decode: 1 new token against a KV cache of capacity C_kv = 64 + max_frames
capacities.acoustic: 3 real tokens padded to one 32-row tile, fixed
capacities.vocode: C_frames = 32 input frames -> 256 output frames, inside the codec stub's 2048-row ALiBi mask

trace_contract.trace_setup_rules: Pin the variable dim to C and PRE-UPLOAD the padded input plus every shape-dependent constant into PERSISTENT device buffers OUTSIDE the trace. Constant VALUES come from the HF reference itself: cos/sin from ref.model.rotary_emb, the additive causal mask from the reference's mask builder, the KV pad at kv_heads x head_dim, the codec ALiBi window masks from each group's own alibi_slopes, and the acoustic 3-of-32 column mask. Padded positions are masked so the output on [0:real_len] is unchanged.
trace_contract.trace_step_rules: ONE host-op-free forward at the fixed shape reading ONLY those persistent buffers. NO from_torch and NO per-call ttnn.zeros/arange inside the trace. KNOWN FIX: flow_matching_audio_transformer's forward calls ttnn.zeros for the 29-row tile pad on every call - that must be hoisted to build time into a persistent buffer before the acoustic stage can be captured.
trace_contract.trace_inputs_rules: ZERO-ARG, returns exactly the argument <stage>_trace_setup takes, assembled from the captured reference tensors under _captured/<name>/ - the same goldens the e2e test and demo use. This is the standard model-agnostic seam; the model-specific assembly lives behind this fixed name. It MUST exist for every stage.

trace_items.prefill: B * C_seq - the 26 blocks process every prompt token of every sample (32 * 64 = 2048)
trace_items.decode: B - one token per sample per step (32)
trace_items.acoustic: n_decoding_steps * 2 * B * 3 = 7 * 2 * 32 * 3 = 1344 - one _trace_step is one FULL frame, and the 3 acoustic blocks see 3 token rows per CFG-doubled batch per Euler step. Priced at 1 item this stage would be given a compute roof ~1344x too small and then misreported as memory-bound.
trace_items.vocode: B * C_frames * 8 = 32 * 32 * 8 = 8192 - the frame count at the decoder's OUTPUT rate. The four transformer groups process C, 2C, 4C and 8C frames respectively (the three transposed convolutions each double the rate), and 8C is what the last group and the output projection retire. Counting the 32 INPUT frames would undercount the repeated blocks by ~3.75x.

trace_contract.ar_decode_contract: decode_prefill(inputs) seeds the resident self-attention KV cache for the whole prompt (there is no cross-attention: the model is decoder-only). decode_step() reads that cache, appends one slot, and NEVER recomputes the prefix.
trace_contract.trace_region_size: sized from the LARGEST stage, which is prefill at C_seq x 26 layers. If a capture overflows, C is shrunk and the fallback is PRINTED - never silently dropped.
trace_contract.selftest: trace_capture_selftest(device): for EACH stage, capture ONE step between ttnn.begin_trace_capture / end_trace_capture, execute_trace it, PCC-check the replay against the reference, then RELEASE the trace before the next stage. Stage traces must not co-reside. Returns True only if every stage captured host-free AND matched.
trace_contract.host_op_selftest: host_op_selftest() runs both task heads' forwards under scripts.tt_hw_planner.host_op_observer.observe_host_ops(), with tokenization and the one-time weight build OUTSIDE the observed region and all model math (encoded inputs -> waveform / token ids, including the prefix embedding and the on-device argmax) INSIDE it. Returns host_op_observer.verdict(ops). Fails if EITHER head fires a host aten op.

layers_knobs.factory: build_pipeline(device, model=None, layers=None, heads=None, **kwargs) is MODULE-LEVEL in tt/pipeline.py and CONSTRUCTS AND RETURNS the resident pipeline object carrying PIPELINE_STAGES and the per-stage hooks. It never runs the model. It accepts and ignores demo kwargs (text, voice, prompt, language, ...) for call-signature compatibility; the resident build derives its shapes from the config, not a prompt.
layers_knobs.layers: the DEFAULT depth for EVERY repeated block. None means every layer - never 0, which a builder would read as a zero-layer model.

stacks.min_reason: the 4 interchangeable block kinds must all stay present, and the structural stack walk needs >= 3 same-typed members
stacks.note: prefill and decode SHARE this one stack (same weights, two phases). Both override names are accepted; the depth is the first non-None of (decode_layers, prefill_layers, layers), and setting both to different values is an ERROR rather than a silent last-wins.

stacks.min_reason: 3 is already the full depth and is also the structural-walk floor

the cap applies to blocks-per-group, floored at 1; all FOUR groups must survive because each carries a different sliding window (2/4/8/16), so capping to 1 per group leaves 4 blocks - which is also above the >= 3 walk floor

layers_knobs.why_one_knob_per_stack: optimize sizes a coverage depth PER STACK - the smallest window in which every distinct op of that stack appears - and those numbers differ. With a single parameter the tool collapses them to the max and every section is profiled at the deepest one. This model is the worked case: a 26-layer text decoder, a 3-block acoustic stack and an 8-block codec stack, and a lone `layers` between them capped the text path while leaving the audio sections at full depth.
layers_knobs.a_capped_build_is_still_a_model: Capping caps how many times a repeated block runs. Embeddings, norms, projectors, the LM head, the codebooks, the convolutions and the de-patch all stay intact, so a capped build still exercises every DISTINCT op the full model runs. If a cap would leave an aggregate sub-block holding zero layers, the build caps to the smallest depth that keeps every stage runnable and PRINTS that it did.
layers_knobs.discoverability: Every repeated stack is held as a plain Python LIST of SAME-TYPED elements. The four text block kinds are different closures, so they are wrapped in a COMMON BASE class (one class, a kind tag, one __call__) and the list elements share a type. The object build_pipeline returns exposes .reference_model, so the HF reference stays reachable as ground truth for how many sections the model has and how deep each is. No base class is required by the walk - it reads any same-typed object with __dict__ - so no __slots__ anywhere on the block classes.
layers_knobs.proving_the_knob_works: optimize caps and re-measures the work signal and reports the knob INERT if the op count does not move. A test in tests/e2e/ builds at layers=4 and at full depth and asserts the built per-stack depths differ as requested, so an ignored cap fails here rather than silently downstream.

tt/: pipeline.py (THE one shared chained pipeline + build_pipeline + PIPELINE_STAGES + trace/host selftests)
common.py (tokenizer, 32-prompt input builder, reference loader bridge, InvocationCounter, stub import/build)
golden.py (HF reference chains - imported by tests and the demo's --compare only)
kernels/ (the custom C++ kernels carried over from the previous round)
tests/e2e/: test_gates.py (Gate 1 + Gate 2 + anti-shortcut scan + layers-knob proof)
package_layout.README.md: what each Call does, how to run it, the measured PCC numbers, the recorded holes
package_layout.one_pipeline_rule: The chained forward pass lives ONLY in tt/. Both the demo entrypoints and the e2e tests import and call the same functions. No wiring is duplicated in demo/ - a second copy would drift from the test and ship a broken demo behind a green test.
package_layout.retired: The previous round's tt/{acoustic,generation,hidden_states}.py and their heads are retired: they import stub names (model, decoder_layer, r_m_s_norm, rotary_embedding, m_l_p) that no longer exist in Source B, and tt/acoustic.py ported the acoustic transformer as causal RoPE MistralDecoderLayers, which Source B's own bidirectional_attention stub shows is wrong on both counts (it is bidirectional and RoPE-free). tt/fast_ops.py's overrides are re-evaluated against the new stubs rather than carried over blind.

holes.detail: The OSS checkpoint ships no input_proj.* or encoder_blocks.* tensors. encode_waveforms raises in the reference itself.
holes.consequence: There is no audio-input task head. text-to-speech is the model's advertised task and is fully covered.

holes.what: The serving prompt template and the interleaved text/audio segmentation
holes.detail: params.json carries codebook_pattern 'parallel' and interleave_{audio,text}_tokens_per_segment 8192, but the loop that applies them lives in vllm-omni, which is not one of the two permitted sources. With both limits at 8192 a short utterance is a single audio segment, so the single-segment chain the pipeline implements is the applicable case.
holes.consequence: Recorded here rather than papered over. A long-form multi-segment chain is out of scope for this run.

holes.detail: The prefill runs causal SDPA without a per-row padding mask, so rows are equalised by left-padding the TEXT segment with BOS tokens (every row still ends on its real final tokens). TT and HF see identical ids, so parity is unaffected; the effect on audio quality is measured by the WER/MOS scores against the HF golden on the SAME ids.
